title: The Search Box Breach
subtitle: A filter returns every tenant’s records

brief.narrative: The API concatenates a user filter into SQL. An attacker changes the query structure with quotes and boolean syntax.
symptoms: Search API metrics diverge from the service-level symptom
The problem reproduces only under the triggering workload
Logs contain enough evidence to distinguish cause from consequence
brief.objective: Identify the root cause, select a production-safe fix, and explain the trade-off.

rootCause.question: Which root cause explains all of the evidence?

options.text: Unbounded queueing and retries turned overload into congestion collapse.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: A dual write to the database and broker was not atomic.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Untrusted input was interpreted as SQL code.
options.feedback: Correct. Escaping by hand is brittle. Parameterization separates code from data, but it does not replace tenant authorization.

options.text: The create operation lacked a stable idempotency key and replayed a committed side effect.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

fix.question: Which fix is safest for production?

options.text: Write the business row and outbox row in one database transaction, relay with retries, and make consumers idempotent.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Use parameterized queries for values, allowlist dynamic identifiers/operators, minimize DB privileges, and test authorization independently.
options.feedback: Correct. Escaping by hand is brittle. Parameterization separates code from data, but it does not replace tenant authorization.

options.text: Require a scoped idempotency key, atomically store request hash and result, return the original result on replay, and reject key reuse with different input.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Set admission limits, bounded queues and deadlines; shed low-priority work, apply retry budgets/backoff, degrade gracefully, and scale from saturation signals.
